added.name: InfraOptimal
added.long_description:
We need more computers faster than we can manufacture chips, while the average GPU workload sits below 50% utilization. 

The answer is not more, it is better use of what we already have. Infraoptimal runs open models as self optimizing inference endpoints: launch any model on your own cloud or ours, and each endpoint is tuned to its model, its workload and the hardware it runs on. Behind it, our agent-driven compiler expands the search space beyond a small set of deterministically discoverable optimizations to functionally equivalent ones, proposing novel methods from state of the art literature and validating them formally, leaving reusable transformations that get better with every program they optimize. We increase speed and throughput while decreasing cost and compute.

long_description.before: Roxels is a vision-enabled voice agent that can handle complex flows for your users. For example, it can onboard and give the “Collison Installation” experience to every customer, not just the first ten.
long_description.after: Trebu is an AI coworker for road freight. Tendering and tracking loads still run on emails, calls and WhatsApp messages between shippers, brokers and carriers. Trebu reads those messages, pulls out load details, matches loads to carriers and handles the back-and-forth until each load is covered. Once a truck is moving, Trebu monitors the shipment, follows up with drivers and flags delays or incidents before they become problems. Ops teams move more freight with fewer people, and every load is tracked in one place from tender to delivery.

long_description.before:
We're building an AI powered platform for engineers that are building new robots and machines. 

We allow users to invent and modify machine designs in a matter of minutes, not years. Ayna and Andy, the co-founders, met during their time at Harvard and started this in 2024 as their programs were wrapping up. We're commercializing 10+ years research done by our team at Harvard and MIT on this space. Our team wrote the very first papers on applying GenAI and optimization algorithms to compose robots from parts and applying computational design to fine tune machine designs. We're bringing in our deep knowledge of modifying equipment and integrating it into factories keenly understanding what makes hardware hard. 

We take in parts under consideration, constraints and tasks at hand and our algorithm formulates and fine tunes from 100s of possible design options. All in a few clicks, so engineers can push hardware to market faster and companies can benefit from the inventions being done by their R&D teams. We already have two paying customers in the OEM and system integrator spaces. 

We are venture backed and supported by a GBP 2.5MM grant by ARIA, the UK Government's invention agency.
long_description.after:
MorphoAI builds hardware foundation models for mechanical engineering. Our GPU-accelerated design models that let engineers generate and explore hundreds of complete mechanical assembly designs in minutes, accelerating the invention of new hardware. Our models learns from a company’s prior CAD designs and generate editable assemblies from engineering requirements, incorporating standard and custom components and manufacturing constraints. This enables companies to design and ship the next generation of their hardware faster and better than competition.

The models can generate assemblies with up to 500 parts in minutes, including a full bill of materials. Engineers can explore 100s of design options at the beginning of a project and refine and validate the outputs within their existing CAD.

MorphoAI’s technology builds on research conducted by its team at MIT and Harvard, with support from ARIA, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency with a GBP 2.5M grant. Its customer list includes companies like ABB and other large OEMs in robotics and automation, electric, power and grid, consumer electronics, and industrial equipment. 

Ayna and Andy, the co-founders, met during their time at Harvard and started this in 2024. Our founding team is built of a prof. of ECE and robotics at Carnegie Mellon, Forbes u30 serial hardware entrepreneur, and an ex. Amazon Robotics scientist. Between them, they have written 65+ papers on algorithms for hardware design during their PhDs at Harvard and MIT. The team at large holds PhDs from Imperial, TU Wein, UCL and has worked across computational geometry, computer vision, ML, optimization, simulation, and the CAD space.

long_description.before:
CONUS structures fragmented medical device information for surgeons. We combine manufacturer documentation, hospital protocols and medical research in one place, giving surgeons and MedTech teams reliable answers across products and procedures.

We already work with leading manufacturers including Johnson & Johnson, Stryker and Zimmer Biomet, and since launching six months ago we’ve gone live in 22 hospitals.

Long term, hospitals will use CONUS to select and order implants across manufacturers.

long_description.before:
Industrial enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected software and machines, with critical knowledge held by a few experienced employees. 

Faraday builds self-improving systems that take on this operational work. We connect to existing software and machines and build training and evaluation environments around each company’s workflows and data.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.
